dedupe_keys.name: moss gpu accelerated large scale open microscopic traffic simulation system

description: MOSS, the MObility Simulation System, is an open-source microscopic traffic simulator from the Tsinghua FIB Lab that runs on GPUs and is described as about a hundred times faster than conventional simulators, so city-wide networks with very many vehicles can be run. The repository documents realistic origin-destination generation with generative methods, map and population inputs in protobuf format, and outputs to AVRO files, a PostgreSQL database or a local directory. The core engine is written in C++ with a Python interface and installs with pip; it needs Linux, CUDA 11.8 or later and Python 3.9 or later. It is MIT licensed and free. Its releases run from v1.0.0 in December 2024 to v1.4.0 in April 2025, which added CO2 emission computation, and the last commit was on 26 August 2025. Caveats: it needs an NVIDIA GPU, no peer-reviewed paper is cited in the README and validation against real counts is left to users. It suits network flow, agent-based and capacity planning studies for urban roads. Related catalogue records: platform-lcsim and model-cityflow are other large-scale traffic simulators.
